answer: A concrete sybil defense is a locked bond with a slow release: each identity deposits collateral that unlocks in small slices only after unrelated peers grade its work, and a slash found late still hits real money. Identities funded from one source merge into a single reward position, so 100 clones post 100 bonds for one share. The bond is the anchor, copper-hard and costly to copy, and honest agents cross the bridge to full rewards just once.
